title: Foreigners Report Thousands of Seoul Taxi Overcharges
paragraphs: Seoul is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Asia, but many foreign visitors have had unpleasant experiences with the city's taxis. According to new data, foreign passengers have reported thousands of cases of overcharging by taxi drivers in recent years.

The figures were released in October 2026 by Mo Gyeong-jong, a member of South Korea's National Assembly, who obtained the data from the Seoul city government. Between 2021 and August 2026, foreign visitors filed 6,481 complaints about being charged too much for taxi rides in the city.

However, only a small number of these complaints led to punishment. Just 204 cases, or 3.1%, resulted in official penalties. These included 176 warnings, 26 suspensions of drivers' licenses and two cases in which licenses were taken away. In another 1,865 cases, drivers were simply given cautions or advice, which have no legal consequences. Meanwhile, the proportion of complaints that could not be properly investigated rose from 38.8% in 2023 to 60.7% in the first eight months of 2026.

According to the city, one of the main problems is that many tourists have already left the country and cannot be contacted. In addition, Seoul offers a reward of 500,000 won to people who report overcharging of foreign visitors, but no one has received this reward since 2021. Mo blamed a lack of publicity and unclear procedures. He said the government must make sure that complaints "backed by clear evidence lead to actual penalties."
Some cases have attracted particular attention. In July 2026, for example, a tourist from Taiwan shared a receipt showing a fare of 690,000 won for a ride from eastern Seoul to Incheon Airport.

The city has been taking steps to address the problem. Since December 2025, taxi receipts have included English, and tourists can report problems using QR codes in taxis and at airports. In addition, from September 2026, stricter penalties have applied, with drivers facing a 30-day suspension for a first offense.
